title: FinTech
body:
**FinTech** covers software replacing the functions of a bank: payment, lending, investment and
the currency itself. The course treats it as the economic block's second half, and the
recurring question is accountability.

```
digital payment      transfer without a bank in the middle of every step
algorithmic lending  a model decides creditworthiness from data about you
crowdfunding         capital raised from many small contributors directly
cryptocurrency       a ledger maintained by agreement, with no institution
robo-advising        portfolio allocation by rule, with no person involved
```

Algorithmic lending is where the ethical weight sits. A loan officer who refuses an application
can be asked why and can be appealed to. A model that refuses it produces a score, and the
reasons are distributed across thousands of weights, so there is frequently no explanation to
give even in principle. The decision is also applied consistently, which sounds like fairness
and means a flaw in the model applies to every applicant at once, where a flawed officer
affected only the people they met.

Cryptocurrency raises the same question about the institution itself. Removing the trusted
intermediary removes the entity that reverses a fraudulent transaction, which is a cost and a
benefit depending on which side of the transaction you are on.

[[CRYPTOGRAPHY]] (MATH 4111) covers the mechanisms underneath, and [[DIRECTED READING]]
(COMP 4299) is the project that built a working financial analysis tool and met these questions
from the implementation side.
